source_text: Hi, I'm asking you to take over on the M-象-2000 mission and develop a compatibility surface with claude-15's work on -40°

fragments.text: Hi, I'm asking you to take over on the M-象-2000 mission and develop a compatibility surface with claude-15's work on -40°

reply_text:
㊥ (take over M-象-2000) Done: I accepted in the bell from claude-15 and the mission's Owner line now reads claude-16 (futon3c c6f2b068). The first job, the false-open ports, is already partly diagnosed, and the diagnosis sets what the compatibility surface with 40ºBelowDB should be. I'll record the findings in a lab note now, then lay out the surface.Dispatched the discovery packet to codex-70 and parked. Checking the job actually started before I report.㊢ (what I did this turn) Took ownership (c6f2b068), wrote the first lab note on the false-open ports (74ac5997), and dispatched a read-only discovery packet to codex-70 (f239bb25), job `invoke-1791691759972-4117-d852b61f`, park `park-7129c1c1`, deadline 45 min. The job is running.

㊬ (false-open ports) Checked this turn against the record files and the live store. Neither the quote matcher nor the adjacency table is the first cause. The replies are missing from the records: 20 of 24 operator turns in claude-15's labelled session have an empty reply text, and so do all 210 analysed turns from 10-09 to 10-10 and every turn before 10-04. No reply acts, so nothing could answer. Where replies do exist, the brackets are labels rather than quotes in 662 of 797 marked paragraphs, and the matcher links only quotes. It links 108 of the 123 quotes it is given. The replies themselves are on the live futon1b as agent-chat evidence, so they can be put back and ports recomputed. The packet to codex-70 measures how completely they map before anyone backfills.

㊭ ("compatibility surface with claude-15's work on -40°") Three contact points, in the order I'd build them.
1. **Same ids, same shapes.** 40ºBelowDB mirrors settled turns into its scratch store. The turn service already writes each settled turn as evidence with id `e-xiang-turn-<record-id>`, and the reply is agent-chat evidence. The follower should mint those ids and bodies, so at switch-over to the live store its writes become quiet duplicates. Ports stay where `compute-ports!` puts them, on the record, and the follower reads them rather than recomputing. claude-15 has already agreed to this in principle.
2. **Memory writes join turns by session and time.** A memory version carries the writing session from the frontmatter stamp. A turn carries its session and created_at. One query over both answers "which turn wrote this memory", with no new record kind in the turn seam. The seam schema stays "what an operator turn is".
3. **Warnings and errors enter as acts.** An Emacs warning or a failed job becomes a `report-problem` act authored by the component, closed by the same table as the operator's (verify, explain, redirect, commit). The record is turn-shaped with origin "system" and no reading. The store side gives it a subject reference, so the -40° open view and the ports share one id. That is the piece claude-15 and I settle together, after the ports are trustworthy.

㊟ (order) Ports first. Until reply text is restored, every open-items view, theirs or mine, counts unanswered turns that were answered. The claude-14 replay also waits on it.

🈯 (one thing to confirm) `constrain` is an opener in the adjacency table, so Joe's standing rules sit in the inbox as debts. I plan to move it to the standings class, answered by in-force rather than by a reply, and to make that a proposal with the labelled rows as the test. Say so if you want it to stay a port.
